description: An interpreter fed its PROGRAM on stdin -- `python3 - <<'PY' ... PY`, `python3 <<EOF ... EOF`, `node - <<'JS'`, `ruby <<'RB'`, `perl <<'PL'`, or the here-string `python3 - <<< "..."` -- is the `-c`/`-e` inline-source shape with a different spelling, and the literal write paths inside the body are read the way the `-c` arm reads them: `open(<lit>, 'w'|'a'|'x')`, `Path(<lit>).write_text|write_bytes|open('w')`, `shutil.copy*|move(_, <lit>)`, `os.rename|replace(_, <lit>)`, plus the existing node/ruby/perl inner patterns. Until 2026-09-06 this was BC-OOS-003 (`PythonHeredocBypass`), filed beside the two-step subprocess class on the claim that only the OUTER call shape is grammar-scanned, never the inner program text. That claim was already false for `-c` (BC-006), and the heredoc body is not file- or stdin-mediated in the sense the OOS class means: it sits between the `<<` operator and its terminator inside the very command string the hook receives, and the mask walker already parses those bounds. Driven 2026-09-06 (DEF-698): the `-c` spelling of the same write denied, `cat > <hook> <<'EOF'` denied, this allowed. Fix: `_INTERP_STDIN_RE` (a `_CMD_POS`-anchored opener matched on the MASKED string, so a `python3 - <<'X'` line inside a quoted-delimiter documentation heredoc or behind a `#` is a mention) feeds `_stdin_program_bodies`, which slices the body out of the RAW command by offset and dispatches it to the interpreter's inner write patterns. Still out of scope, by the same boundary the `-c` arm has: computed paths (variables, f-strings, argv); a body that is DATA to a script or module operand (`python3 script.py <<EOF`, `python3 -m json.tool <<EOF`); a valued flag before the `-` operand; a file-mediated two-step write (BC-OOS-001). The PowerShell tool has no heredoc; its stdin spelling is a pipe into the interpreter, covered by BC-052 (DEF-712, 2026-09-08) -- the twin this row scoped out toward the permission-verb row is closed.
